newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai army on alert to bar Cambodian refugee influx.
newsitem.headline: Thai army on alert to bar Cambodian refugee influx.

text.p: Truckloads of Thai troops armed with mortars and machine guns reinforced the border on Thursday to prevent thousands of Cambodians from crossing into Thailand to flee fighting, witnesses said.

Witnesses from the Cambodian town of O'Smach, only a barbed wire border fence from here, said the sound of gunfire was clearly audible indicating that Cambodian strongman Hun Sen's soldiers were nearing the town, the last significant stronghold of royalist forces opposing Hun Sen.

"We heard that Hun Sen troops have already overrun Pha-Oung village about 10 km (seven miles) from O'Smach town and people who live on the outskirts of the town are now crowding at the gate and at the centre of the town," one witness said.
It was not possible to enter the town to confirm the report.

It was believed to be the first time Thai forces had deployed mortars in the area since Hun Sen's troops pushed back soldiers loyal to ousted Cambodian prime minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh to the area in recent weeks.
A Thai army source who was monitoring the fighting inside Cambodia said the refugees were very frightened and poised to try to cross the border.
"I think we (Thai army) may have to allow them in later today or tonight," an army officer who asked not to be identified told Reuters.

Forces loyal to strongman Hun Sen have been inching their way toward O'Smach, firing mortar rounds inside the town for the first time on Wednesday. Their advance has been slowed by booby traps and landmines lain by retreating Ranariddh forces.
Since ousting Ranariddh on July 6 Hun Sen has battled the prince for diplomatic approval overseas while pushing the ragged remnants of his army to remote pockets of the country.
Only O'Smach and a few villages remain in the hands of forces opposing Hun Sen, some of them controlled by the rump of the Khmer Rouge which ruled Cambodia between 1975 and 1979.
